contents.text: We currently recognize 118 elements, each with distinct physical and chemical properties. But our understanding of the elements has changed significantly over time. Up until the late 1700s, most scientists' understanding came from ancient Greek philosophy or the alchemical theory that matter was made of only mercury, sulfur, and salt. However, these concepts were based on ideas rather than scientific experimentation.

pieces.text: In 1783, French chemist Antoine Lavoisier observed that water could be made by combining two gases, which he named oxygen and hydrogen. According to Lavoisier, these gases were simple substances, or
, that could not be chemically broken down.

textContent.text: Unlike many scientists before him, Lavoisier used experiments to determine if a substance was an element. In 1789, he published a list of 33 elements grouped into four categories according to their properties. His list included elements still recognized today like hydrogen, oxygen, sulfur, and copper, as well as substances no longer recognized as elements such as heat and light.
